content.text: In regions where platforms like Stripe and PayPal are unavailable, digital creators face significant barriers to [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-payment-explained-digital-16|COREMERCH guide to automated]] commerce. This is particularly true in Nigeria and Ghana, where conventional payment [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/solutions-when-stripe-paypal-ban-account-which-architecture-15|Solutions When]] fail to deliver. The [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-11|architecture]] behind Google Apps Script offers a robust alternative for automating digital product delivery and payment processing, ensuring creators can efficiently manage their sales without relying on restricted financial services.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Google apps

Google Apps Script serves as a powerful tool for automating tasks in digital commerce, especially when integrated with crypto payment systems. This architecture allows for seamless processing of orders and instant delivery of digital products. It matters because it empowers creators who have been locked out of traditional payment systems, providing them with the means to operate independently and effectively in a global marketplace.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture consists of Google Apps Script, which acts as the backend processing engine, paired with NOWPayments for handling crypto transactions. When a customer makes a purchase, NOWPayments triggers a webhook that communicates with Google Apps Script. This script processes the payment confirmation, retrieves order details, and automates the delivery of digital products. A well-configured stack can handle this entire process in under 30 seconds, ensuring a swift transaction experience for the customer.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This setup is designed for digital creators in countries where traditional payment processors are inaccessible. Creators selling ebooks, courses, and digital assets need a reliable system for order fulfillment that doesn't depend on intermediaries. By leveraging this architecture, they gain full control over their sales processes, ensuring they can reach customers without the hindrance of payment restrictions. This infrastructure not only provides a solution but also fosters independence and creativity.
Automating digital commerce frees you from platform dependencies.
The Components That Make It Work Together

Key components of this architecture include Google Apps Script for backend logic, NOWPayments for crypto payment processing, and a storage solution like Supabase or Google Sheets for order management. These elements work in harmony to automate the fulfillment of digital products. For instance, when a payment is confirmed via NOWPayments, the corresponding webhook initiates a script in Google Apps Script that retrieves the order from Supabase, allowing for immediate product delivery to the customer.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this architecture effectively, start by setting up a Google Apps Script project and linking it with NOWPayments. Next, configure your webhook to ensure it triggers on payment confirmations. Utilize Supabase or Google Sheets for storing order data. Finally, test the entire process end-to-end to ensure smooth operation before going live. For a comprehensive solution, consider the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) to expedite setup and ensure robust functionality.
How does automated digital product delivery work with crypto payments?

The webhook secret is the security mechanism that prevents fake webhook injection. NOWPayments signs every webhook with an HMAC hash using the secret key you configured in your account. Your backend recomputes the hash using the same secret key and the raw webhook body. If the hashes match, the webhook is legitimate. If they do not match, the request is rejected before any order processing occurs. This validation happens in under one millisecond. Combined with the independent on-chain transaction verification that follows, it creates a two-layer security model that makes fraudulent order injection effectively impossible against a correctly configured sovereign stack.
A properly configured stack processes orders in under 30 seconds.

Your Deployment Checklist

First, create a Google Apps Script project to handle backend logic. Next, sign up for NOWPayments and configure your webhook for payment notifications. Set up a Supabase or Google Sheets account to store order details. Ensure your script retrieves and processes orders accurately upon webhook triggers. Finally, conduct thorough testing to confirm that digital products are delivered as intended before launch.
Frequently Asked Questions
How does automated digital product delivery work with crypto payments?

Automated delivery functions through webhooks that trigger upon payment confirmation. When a payment is made, NOWPayments notifies Google Apps Script, which processes the order and sends the product link to the customer automatically.
What is a webhook and how does it trigger order fulfillment?

A webhook is a method for one application to send real-time data to another when a specific event occurs. In this context, it triggers order fulfillment by notifying Google Apps Script when a payment is confirmed by NOWPayments.
Can I automatically send download links after a crypto payment confirms?
Yes, once the payment is confirmed, the webhook sends the order details to Google Apps Script, which then automatically sends the download link to the customer via email.
What is the role of Cloudflare Workers in this setup?

Cloudflare Workers can enhance the performance of your application by handling requests and responses quickly. They can also manage the webhook events, ensuring that your application scales efficiently without worrying about server limitations.
How can I ensure my delivery process is reliable?

To ensure reliability, test the entire flow from payment to product delivery. Use a staging environment to simulate real transactions and monitor webhook responses for accuracy before deploying to production.
Cloudflare Workers can handle up to 100,000 webhook events daily on the free tier.
